query: What review signals predict low Yelp user satisfaction?

per_column.name: negative_word_count
per_column.rationale: Count of negative words is derived from review_text, not from the label, and plausibly carries strong signal about negative sentiment predicting low satisfaction.

per_column.name: complaint_phrase_count
per_column.rationale: Complaint phrases in the text are a legitimate external signal correlated with dissatisfaction, not a restatement of the label.

per_column.name: exclamation_mark_count
per_column.rationale: Punctuation intensity is a text feature that can carry emotional signal (positive or negative); plausibly predictive though weaker.

per_column.name: excessive_caps_flag
per_column.rationale: Caps usage signals heightened emotion often tied to complaints; a legitimate text-derived predictor outside the label.

per_column.name: review_word_length
per_column.rationale: Review length is a generic but legitimate text feature that can correlate with satisfaction (e.g., longer venting reviews); modest signal.

per_column.name: comparison_mentioned_flag
per_column.rationale: Mentioning comparisons to alternatives is a content signal that can indicate dissatisfaction; a valid external predictor.

per_column.name: refund_or_pricing_complaint_flag
per_column.rationale: Flagging refund/pricing complaints is a targeted content signal strongly associated with dissatisfaction, derived from text not the label.

judge.rationale: All seven columns are text-derived features that lie outside label_pos and none leak or restate the outcome. The strongest (negative_word_count, complaint_phrase_count, refund_or_pricing_complaint_flag) carry genuine, targeted signal for predicting low satisfaction. Others (exclamation_mark_count, excessive_caps_flag, review_word_length, comparison_mentioned_flag) are more generic/shallow but still plausibly correlated. As a set they give solid predictive leverage, though several are sparse binary flags with few positives, limiting incremental value beyond the raw text.
